introHeading: Wedding photo booths built for Brooklyn receptions
introParas: Your photographer captures the ceremony and the portraits. The booth captures what happens after — the cousins piling in six at a time, the great-aunt who commandeered the boa, the friends who come back for a third round once the band picks up. We have carried that setup into Bushwick warehouse freight elevators, up the narrow stairs of Park Slope brownstones, and onto Williamsburg rooftops with the skyline behind the backdrop, and we plan the load-in around your specific venue before we ever show up with road cases.

The mirror booth is what most Brooklyn couples book, because the full-length format handles a whole wedding party at once and works for guests from age eight to eighty — a real consideration at the multigenerational receptions common in Bay Ridge and Crown Heights. For a black-tie affair in a Downtown Brooklyn loft or gallery space, the glam booth's black-and-white look tends to match the room better than a color print. If your crowd skews younger — a Greenpoint or Bushwick reception where half the guest list will post before the cake is cut — the 360 booth is the one that gets used all night. Past about 150 guests, we usually suggest pairing whichever static booth you pick with a roaming attendant so the seated tables get covered instead of everyone converging on one line.

On the logistics side: we carry a $2 million policy and turn your venue's certificate of insurance around the same day you send us their contact, which matters because most Brooklyn venues ask for one before they'll confirm your floor plan. We arrive an hour ahead of your start time and are set up in about 20 minutes, in a 10ft x 10ft footprint when the room allows it or as tight as 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance when it doesn't — a real question at some of the converted warehouse spaces in Bushwick and Gowanus. And there's no travel fee anywhere in Brooklyn, quoted from your venue's ZIP code before you ever book.

faqHeading: Wedding Photo Booth in Brooklyn — FAQ

faqs.q: How many hours should we book for a Brooklyn wedding?
faqs.a: Three to four hours covers most receptions. Tell us your run sheet — including your Brooklyn venue's curfew, since some loft and warehouse spaces cut music earlier than a traditional catering hall — and we'll suggest a start time rather than sell you hours you don't need.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee for Brooklyn weddings?
faqs.a: No. There's no travel fee anywhere in Brooklyn — from Bay Ridge to Greenpoint — and we confirm that in writing before you book, not as a surprise line on the invoice.

faqs.q: Can the booth handle a loading dock or freight elevator situation?
faqs.a: Yes, and in Brooklyn it's the norm rather than the exception. We've loaded road cases up through Bushwick warehouse freight elevators and up narrow Park Slope brownstone stairwells. Tell us your venue and we'll ask about access ahead of time so it's not a surprise on the day.

faqs.q: Which booth works best for a Brooklyn wedding?
faqs.a: The mirror booth is the most-booked, since it handles a full wedding party and works across every generation in the room. For a black-tie loft or gallery wedding in Downtown Brooklyn, the glam booth's editorial look tends to fit better. For a younger Williamsburg or Bushwick crowd, the 360 booth gets used hardest.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the booth need?
faqs.a: Optimal is a 10ft x 10ft footprint, with 8ft x 8ft and 7.5ft of ceiling clearance as the minimum — a real question in some of Brooklyn's converted warehouse and loft venues. We also need a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet that isn't shared with the DJ or catering.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and can you get there early?
faqs.a: About 20 minutes once we arrive, and we build in a full hour before your scheduled start so everything is tested before your first guest walks in. If your venue needs us on site earlier than that, idle time is $55 per hour.

faqs.q: Can you get a certificate of insurance to our Brooklyn venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $2 million policy and turn COIs around the same day you send us your venue's contact — most Brooklyn spaces want this on file before they'll finalize your floor plan.

faqs.q: Do we get every photo from the night, not just the prints?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image lands in an online gallery you can download in full and share with your guests, on top of the unlimited prints handed out at the reception.
